title: Cab Calloway's 1934 tour of Britain and Paris
summary: The band played the London Palladium, Scotland, Manchester and a Paris concert; a jealous pit band blasted distortions, and the band tore the theater up.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now you left Cab, was it '35 or '36?
I left Cab between '38 and '39. Mostly '39. '39.
Oh, I see, no, what I was thinking about, you went to Europe with Cab --
Yes, '34, we went to Europe, played there.
Well we played the Palladium in London.
And we went to Scotland and we played in Scotland, and that's about all. Manchester.
The British Isles, so you didn't go to the Continent?
And we played Paris, we had a concert in Paris at the Salle Pleyel (Unintelligible).

And we also played -- we played a couple of theaters there, we did another theater, I think it was a benefit in London, I don't remember the name of the theater. We -- the pit band at this theater, they give us a hard time before we went on, because they announced Cab's band as a benefit. The pit band started making all kinds of noise with their horns, blowing all kind of distortions that was to welcome us, the band. It was a very lousy thing they did.
Oh, you mean they were jealous?

Well, either that or they were just sort of giving us a hard time, I don't know. They just started blasting all kinds of distortions with their horns and then we came on and do it and we tore up the theater, man. Tore it up. So that gave us some sort of encouragement. We say well what those guys doing down there. So baby when that show went on and tore the theater up.
